title: Portfolio site in a weekend
promise: Prepare your images, design the page, write a little HTML and put it online for free.
audience: Designers, photographers and developers who need somewhere to point people

steps.title: Edit your best work
steps.why: GIMP is a full image editor for cropping, color correction and export, and it is free and open source.

steps.title: Shrink the files
steps.why: Squoosh compresses images in the browser and shows before and after side by side, so you can pick the smallest file that still looks right.

steps.title: Design the page
steps.why: Figma's free tier is enough to lay out a single page and decide what goes where before you write any code.

steps.title: Write the page
steps.why: Visual Studio Code is a free editor with good HTML and CSS support, and a portfolio can be a handful of static files.

steps.title: Put it online
steps.why: GitHub Pages serves a repository of static files for free, at a github.io address or your own domain.
